correctness.rationale: Complete combinatorial enumeration gives 111375 ordinary simplices, matching-size distribution (30,375,2540,10155,24474,34805,27300,10260,1400,36). Every pivot pairing is a facet relation; ten cancellations have a uniquely verified alternating gradient path. A global topological sort of all 666330 face incidences proves the final 55626-pair Morse matching acyclic, with one critical 0-cell, five 5-cells and 117 6-cells. The signed integer Morse boundary from the 117 six-cells to the five five-cells is computed explicitly as a zero 5-by-117 matrix. Hurewicz identifies every attaching homotopy class with its degree vector; every six-cell therefore attaches trivially, proving the wedge homotopy type. Independent matching-polynomial recurrence and full F2 boundary rank computations agree. No unproved asymptotic claim is made.

broader_coverage.reasoning: No inspected stronger theorem determines the stated two sphere multiplicities for GP(10,2). The dodecahedral graph is three-vertex-connected on twenty vertices and cannot be outerplanar, since nontrivial outerplanar graphs have connectivity at most two. It is not the categorical product of two paths, which is bipartite, whereas the dodecahedron contains five-cycles. Connectivity bounds for claw-free line graphs do not imply exact homotopy types.

value.rationale: The dodecahedral graph is a canonical cubic Platonic graph. Its ordinary matching complex is a natural topological object with 111375 nonempty faces. The complete integral wedge type resolves torsion and all six-cell attaching maps, questions not answered by the closest exact mod-two homology calculation. The exact five/five-dimensional and 117/six-dimensional sphere multiplicities are mathematically interpretable invariants and the Morse certificate compresses a large natural complex. No classification of a broad family is needed for this intrinsically motivated complete finite calculation.
